anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing moved on this case: both outputs render a first menu of cleanup=1 (recommended) and stop=2 last with no own-merge coverage rows and show evidence only in the hint line, both run the landed guards before the override steps, both remove the reused .worktrees/pr-212 and `branch -D csv-export`, and both emit `gh issue close '210' --comment "Delivered in https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/212, merged 9f1c2d3e4b5a6978."` with the # stripped and the sha substituted from the merge digest. The only textual difference worth noting is that After drops the `-R acme/widgets` flag from the close command; that is harmless here because the command runs from the primary checkout, but if the shared menus.md template is meant to be portable, keeping the explicit `-R <owner/repo>` in the rendered command (or stating that cwd resolves the repo) would make f3 robust to runs started outside the checkout. The 'This PR was already merged before the run (sha)' line and the 'Pick one:' header are a clean way to signal the closed-PR overlay without adding rows, and the re-rendered post-cleanup menu correctly leaves only stop with show evidence still in the hint.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept: the close command still resolves the merge-sha to 9f1c2d3e4b5a6978 and passes '210' and the full comment as separate arguments, and the cleanup path still removes the reused worktree and deletes csv-export. The only movement is f4, and it moves the intended way: Before rendered show evidence as numeric row 2 (so the first menu was cleanup/show evidence/stop rather than cleanup/stop), while After renders exactly cleanup=1 [recommended] and stop=2 last, relegates show evidence to the hint line, carries no own-merge coverage rows, and the numeric cleanup pick runs the landed guard (merge-base --is-ancestor <merge-sha> HEAD after the pull). Two small wording points worth tightening without touching any fact: the `PRIMARY='<scratch>'` placeholder in After is misleading since the fixture identifies the primary checkout concretely (Before's '$PRIMARY denotes the primary checkout identified in the fixture' is clearer), and the post-cleanup menu's single stop row could keep the 'end the gate without further changes' phrasing so the terminal state reads as unchanged rather than merely 'attempted'.
